source_scope: 15 selected production, ABI, adapter, test and build inputs match the Linux workspace byte-for-byte. Not a hermetic whole-worktree release manifest.

execution.runtime: root native host CLI and product BPF, real native dual-stack UDP echo peers; no protocol-server conformance claim
execution.build_location: remote Linux unprivileged temporary Docker build
execution.earlier_development_evidence: 20261113-product-udp-boundaries; not counted as accepted final runs on the current kernel or strengthened sequence

findings.change: Complete the strengthened boundary campaign and source-bound evidence after interrupted validation. Native workers assert actual I/O and retained prefix/length/direction metadata; no product facts are filled from the oracle.
observed_limits: Large-payload I/O is complete at native peers, but product facts retain only the first 128 bytes.
Server/client socket identity and port metadata are retained; full endpoint IP addresses and PID lineage are not added.
Descendant-cgroup coverage does not imply exclusive locks across overlapping ancestor/descendant collectors.

validation.status_validation_scope: Catalog consistency and declared GUI target coverage, not overall product readiness or maturity promotion.
validation.clippy_command: cargo --config profile.dev.package.gewyvern.opt-level=2 clippy --locked --test production_capture_linux_tdd --test native_validation_harness_tdd -- -D warnings

limits: Direct IPv4/IPv6 loopback UDP on one physical host/kernel update; not physical-interface or minimum-kernel certification.
Not fragmentation/reassembly, IPv6 extension headers, GSO/GRO, checksum-verification or high-throughput proof.
The 128-byte cap is intentional: loss-free accounting does not mean complete packet archival. Full native-I/O hashes are not full captured-payload hashes for longer messages.
Native echo peers are not DNS/SNMP/NTP/STUN server conformance or vulnerability detection. No PID attribution, full IP endpoint retention or cross-window transaction claim.
Scope exclusion is tested for sockets created outside the selected hierarchy and for another UDP port. This does not establish a product per-socket allowlist.
The lifecycle regression's induced losses remain incomplete and separate from the loss-free boundary runs. SIGKILL cannot produce complete final counters.
No release-artifact, protocol-count or status-maturity promotion. Earlier development attempts are retained separately.
